chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Illinois Jacquet sessions and Sir Charles Thompson's 'Robin's Nest' blowup
summary: Collins played on Jacquet's records; when J. J. Johnson wrote a Robin's Nest follow-up, Sir Charles walked out and they recorded without piano.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: (Inaudible) Who else did you record with
During that time? Let's see. I recorded with so -- I recorded quite a bit -- I did almost all of Dizzy's recordings. I did all of Illinois Jacquet's recordings. That's another story. Yeah.
Well, we would record say at night. They would turn the lights out, there was no music involved, they'd turn the lights out and distribute the bottles around. And see --
But that was a great little band. It was J. J., Joe Newman, Sir Charles, Al Lucas, Shadow Wilson, and the baritone player Leo --

-- Bill Parker. And I would augment you know -- they would get me to record with them on all of their records, and they had a big hit at this time called Robin's Nest, written by Sir Charles. So Jacquet got J. J. to do another tune, told him to write a tune, and J. J. -- they wanted to follow up on "Robin's Nest" but they didn't ask Sir Charles to do the writing, they asked J. J. to do it. So we're in here and getting ready to record, and J. J. passed this music out, and we play it and it was just like "Robin's Nest" but with just a little different melody, and Sir Charles

jumped up from the piano and called everybody a mother fucker and walked out. And until today we talk about it. He was with [Miles] about a week ago and he was still fuming. That happened 20 years ago, you know.
But that was a great band.
